name: Signal mirror
summary: A flash of aimed sunlight visible for tens of kilometres — the highest-reach signal you can carry in a pocket.
time: seconds, whenever the sun is out

steps.text: Hold the mirror close to your face and sight the target — aircraft, boat, ridge, vehicle — just over the top edge.
Hold your other hand out at arm's length with the target framed in a V between two fingers.
Flash the reflected spot of light onto your own outstretched hand first, then walk the spot into the V.
steps.why: You cannot see where a reflected beam is going. Bouncing it onto something you CAN see is the only way to aim it.

steps.text: With a purpose-made mirror, use the aiming hole: the bright dot you see through it IS where the beam is landing.
Sweep slowly across the horizon when you have no specific target — a searcher may see you before you see them.

verify: You can see the spot of light land on your own hand. Until you can, you are not aiming, you are hoping.
An aircrew that has seen you usually changes course or rocks its wings.
limits: No sun, no signal. It is useless at night, under overcast, and in fog.
It signals presence and direction. It carries no information beyond 'a person is here'.
cautions: Do not flash a pilot continuously once they have clearly seen you — sustained glare in the cockpit is dangerous. Signal, then stop.
The same is true for a vehicle driver on a road below you.
